It is understandable to feel anxious about the possibility of forced treatment. In most places, a therapist cannot simply force a client into an eating disorder treatment center against their will. Involuntary admission is generally considered a last resort and involves a strict legal and medical process. It typically only happens if a person is in immediate, severe, and life-threatening medical danger—such as acute organ failure or severe malnutrition—and is deemed unable to make safe decisions for themselves. 

Because laws regarding involuntary holds vary significantly by location, a therapist usually has to work with medical doctors, hospitals, or the legal system to initiate this process; they cannot do it alone. If you are worried about this, it can be very helpful to share your fears directly with your therapist. Their primary goal is almost always to work collaboratively with you to keep you safe and support your recovery in the least restrictive environment possible.
